initial_count.note: Regulars enrolled for credit or loyalty in a neighbourhood épicerie of ~170 baskets a day.

marketing_consent_share.note: Processing consent is universal among enrolled customers; marketing is the one people refuse.

objection_share.note: A few objectors, so the downgrade path (D-043) has data to test against.

cover_days.note: Days of base demand on the shelf on day one, rounded up to whole cartons.

remaining_shelf_life.note: Fraction of shelf life left on opening batches; they were delivered before the history starts.

weekday_factors.note: Friday–Saturday weekend: Thursday evening restock, Friday dips around the prayer.

normal.note: Morning bread-and-milk run, noon bump, evening peak after work.

friday.note: Busy morning, closed around the Friday prayer.

ramadan.note: Inverted rhythm: late opening, pre-iftar peak 16–18h, closed at iftar, second wave after tarawih.

aid.note: Open only in the afternoon, after family visits.

ramadan.note: Dates as announced in Algeria for 1446 and expected for 1447; both confirmed by Hakim (14/09/2026).

stock_up_days.note: Households stock up the week before Ramadan (D-046 §15).

post_aid_quiet_days.note: The week after Aïd el-Fitr is quiet: pantries are full and budgets spent.

events.note: Aïd al-Adha 2025 as celebrated in Algeria, 2026 as expected; both confirmed by Hakim (14/09/2026). Rentrée dates approximate. Profiles set the demand effect.

spike_last_days_of_month.note: D-046 §17: the spike covers roughly the last two days of the month…

pre_payday_days.note: The week before the spike, when on-account buying rises.

trough_last_day.note: Ends before the pre-payday week of the shortest month.

effects.note: Multipliers on demand, basket size and the share of on-account payments, per phase.

basket_units.note: Weights of a basket of 1 … 50 units (Hakim, 14/09): rising to 7, mirrored down to 13, then a thin tail to 50. P(<7) = 0.45, P(7) = 0.10, P(>7) = 0.45; mean 7.2; about 1 basket in 400 has 40 or more. ~420 units a day make ~58 baskets. The pay cycle scales the drawn size.

substitution_by_tier.note: Chance an out-of-stock line is bought as another variant of the same product: another size of pasta, yes; another brand of coffee, rarely.

payment_shares.note: Hakim, 14/09: overwhelmingly cash, a few CIB/Edahabia cards, rare BaridiMob. The tender for whatever store credit and on-account (the mess section) do not cover.

customer_attach_share.note: Hakim, 14/09: 15–20% of baskets are rung up against an enrolled regular. Regulars differ in how often they come.

opening_float.note: DZD in the drawer at opening: enough change for the morning.

memory_days.note: The shopkeeper's sense of a product's pace is the last two weeks of what sold, stockout days included, which is exactly the bias a naive rule has.

reorder_cover_days.note: Eyeball threshold: reorder when the shelf plus what is on order would last about four days.

order_up_to_cover_days.note: Order enough for about twelve days, rounded up to whole cartons.

slow_mover_rate.note: Products selling under ~2 a week are not watched: reordered only when the shelf is empty.

ramadan_over_order.note: Before Ramadan the shopkeeper orders half as much again as usual, across the board.

ramadan_lookahead_days.note: Over-ordering starts two weeks before Ramadan and stops when it begins.

late_delivery_max_days.note: A delivery comes on its stated lead time or up to two days late, on time being the most likely.

fill_rate.note: Most order lines arrive in full; distributors run short on the rest.

short_delivery_fraction.note: A short line brings between none and most of its cartons.

delivered_shelf_life.note: Delivered stock is fresh: 80–100% of its shelf life remaining.

visit_minutes_after_opening.note: The distributor's representative passes mid-morning on the supplier's delivery days and takes the order.

delivery_window_minutes.note: Deliveries land in the first three hours after opening.

discount_line_share.note: About one line in fifty gets a discount: a regular, a short date, a gesture.

void_share.note: One basket in a hundred is rung wrongly, voided and rung again.

return_line_share.note: Returns are rare in an épicerie: a spoiled yoghurt, a wrong size.

restock_share.note: Most returned goods cannot be sold again.

store_credit_refund_share.note: A regular is often refunded in store credit rather than cash.

store_credit_use_share.note: A regular holding credit usually spends it on the next basket.

on_account_share.note: A regular's basket goes on the tab (le carnet) this often in an ordinary week; calendar.payday.effects scales it up before payday.

paid_out_daily_chance.note: Cash taken from the drawer for small purchases a couple of times a week.

paid_out_amount.note: DZD: bread for the shop, a repair, a delivery tip.

paid_in_daily_chance.note: The float is occasionally topped up at opening.

drop_threshold.note: At the midday break, cash beyond 20,000 DZD above the float goes to the safe.

cash_count_discrepancy_chance.note: About one close in twelve counts wrong.

cash_count_discrepancy_max.note: DZD either way, in 5 DZD steps: change given wrongly, a note miscounted.

count_interval_days.note: One subcategory is counted before opening once a week, in turn.

count_shrinkage_chance.note: A counted lot is found short by a unit or a few: theft, breakage, a mis-scan never corrected.

count_found_chance.note: Occasionally a unit turns up that the system did not know about.

enrolled_share.note: Most regulars have a page in the carnet; a newcomer or someone who once failed to pay does not.

credit_limit.note: DZD: a few days to two weeks of a family's groceries, set by how well the shopkeeper knows them.

never_settle_share.note: A few tabs are never paid; the limit is what stops them growing.

payday_repayment_daily_chance.note: Most tabs are settled in the payday spike (calendar.payday): about nine in ten within its week.

other_repayment_daily_chance.note: Some settle whenever they have the money.

partial_repayment_share.note: A quarter of repayments clear only half the tab, so some debt ages past a pay cycle.

drain_interval_minutes.note: sync-design §10.2: the idle poll. Backoff after a failure is not modelled; the cap (5 min) is close to this interval.

batch_size.note: sync-design §10.3: 500 events a round trip, with no separate catch-up mode.

flaky_link_up_share.note: A consumer 4G router: up about seven hours in ten, hour by hour.

offline_start_day.note: An outage early in June, away from Ramadan.

offline_days.note: sync-design §10.3's own example: three weeks offline.

staples.note: Pasta, couscous, oil, margarine: steady, stocked up before Ramadan.

ramadan_staples.note: Chorba and hrira base: vermicelli, chickpeas, tomato paste, semolina, sugar.

ramadan_cooking.note: Smen, cream, tuna, olives, harissa: bourek and iftar dishes.

ramadan_sweets.note: Halwa chamia, honey, syrups, orange-blossom water.

ramadan_baking.note: Flour and glucose for Aïd cakes, baked in the last days of Ramadan.

ramadan_fresh.note: Lben at the iftar table, and in summer.

dairy_fresh.note: Yoghurt: slightly up in summer and at suhur.

beverages_summer.note: Sodas and energy drinks: heat, iftar and family gatherings.

snacks.note: Biscuits, chips, chocolate: daytime impulse buys fall while fasting.

spices.note: Ras el hanout, cumin: Ramadan cooking and the Aïd al-Adha meat.

coffee_tea.note: Hot drinks: winter, Ramadan evenings, Aïd visits.

breakfast.note: Cereals and chocolate powder: school breakfasts, none during the fast.

baby.note: Baby food and nappies do not follow the calendar.

hygiene.note: Soap, shampoo, paper: a small pre-Ramadan stock-up.

cleaning.note: The house is cleaned top to bottom before Ramadan and before Aïd al-Adha.
